title: Important news
content:
Hi. As you may know, I've made several announcements lately, but I forgot to mention something.

I actually couldn't decide whether to do it or not, but now it's very clear to me. I know I've been mediocre in the past, but I keep working to be a better version of myself. And, above all, I've learned that I need to take my time with things. As the months go by I'm much more patient. That's why, temporarily, the TEKO DEMO won't be visible on the store.

I'm currently doing a complete overhaul of the DEMO so it matches the full game exactly (but with limited content). The reason I don't want more people playing the current version is because it's full of bugs and is way too different from the EA: The EA version is truly incomparable, it's far better than the demo... so that difference means I'm sabotaging myself and generating defamation for my own game. Since the demo is bad, the result is counterproductive; rather than promoting the full version, it drives new players away. I made a huge mistake. I shouldn't have left such an immature demo up.

But well, that's how I learn. With mistakes, because nobody taught me. It's simply a matter of time before everything gets much better.

At the same time, I want you to know that I'm working very hard. As you've probably seen, after finishing TEKO's base content, I've been working in the shadows. I'm progressing very fast. And when I have news, I'm going to need your help to thoroughly test everything before making the version public.

u9.0 is going to be the biggest rework. It's crazy. I can't give too many spoilers, as I feel it's unnecessary; I want to save the surprise for the end. I can only assure you that everything is going to change. It will even be shocking at first, and it'll take players some time to get used to the change. This is going to be extreme.

And, based on the lessons I've learned from my past failures, I understand I need to take my time. I haven't felt burnt out for several days. This is a good sign. I'm starting to recover after pushing myself so hard. Right now I feel really good. I'm making a lot of significant changes, but without any pressure.

The only thing that worries me sometimes is that players might suffer because I'm inexperienced. There are many reasons why, due to my shortcomings in development, a player might not have a good time. Especially in the aesthetics, there are a lot of flaws. But there are also people who might complain about the balance (even though u8.0 is very forgiving).

But, at least I offer dialogue all the time, and that's my biggest strength: the connection with the community. That's why, if you have questions, want help to become a better player, or simply want to give feedback or chat, I can help you out on the Discord server.

I'm not going to promise anything, that would be absurd. I don't know what life has in store for me. The only thing I know is that right now I'm working many hours a day, and not only that, I have it in mind to make this a definitive project, something that is finished. I can't guarantee it, but that's what I'm thinking right now. And the players who have tried the EA version already know where this is heading; it's obvious the potential shines through.

So, that's what I wanted to tell you today: I'm highly focused on u9.0, which will take quite a while to come out but will be worth it and will be a historic milestone in TEKO's development; and, for the time being, the Demo won't be available (I'm really sorry, but it's for everyone's own good and it will pay off in the long run).

The next step after u9.0 is creating new graphical assets outside the game, like trailers, screenshots, a new description—basically an aesthetic revamp.

I don't want to hype you up any more. There are still many weeks to go. I hope you can join me in this, I swear this is my life, I only think about this, I love TEKO. And I'm happy that you're also slowly falling in love with this project. Thanks for everything.

I just fixed all the unlock conditions for the Cards that unlock when beating specific difficulties in certain Pockets.

I did a quick but huge nerf to the Mods.
Pipe/Hat Common Mods: REMOVED.
Pipe/Hat Rare Mods: +2 extra base > +1 extra base.

I made a giant mistake that I knew was going to end badly: adding too much stuff. In the past, I really wanted to add more Mod variety, and the ones that were hardest to create were the new Common Mods, so I decided to add a lower tier of Pipe/Hat, but now I see the results of that decision: the game completely broke. That's why I just did what I knew I had to do from the very beginning. I let it slide, I thought it wouldn't be abused this much, but... XD. For the sake of the game, I prefer having less variety but keeping everything more balanced. TEKO was unfairly forgiving.
Fixed a minor bug. Winning a run with Jean Pocket D4 used to unlock The Transgressor Card. This was not intended; it should be unlocked by winning with Drab Pocket D4.

I just fixed a small visual bug where texts weren't displaying correctly for any language, specifically when using the juice Consumables. When this happens, instead of the normal text, "KEY_NOT_FOUND" appears. I'm letting you know so that if it happens, you can report it correctly. When this text appears as a placeholder, it's because a localization text is missing or it was declared incorrectly.

I just fixed the issues related to having Sinister Cards and managing slot space. For example, now we'll be able to use Consumables like Mask or Binoculars even if we have more than 12 Cards. Previously, the system detected that if we had more Cards than slots, it wouldn't let us receive any new Cards, but this system changed with the new Sinister Cards that don't take up slots. It's been fixed now. I did the same with the Potentially Suspicious Man Card, which generated a Card every time you entered the shop.

u8.0.0!
I've created 13 new Mods.
4 Common / 4 Rare / 5 Pro.

Fixes:
  • Now the amount of Mod slots on each Relic will be retained when exiting/entering a run to avoid any kind of bug or exploit.
  • Ticket (Consumable) won't allow expanding Sinister Cards or Cards with more than 4 slots.
  • Now the description for ultranumber/numberless appears in the Stickers tooltips in the shop and inventory.
It seems like a small patch, especially because I released it fast. But, believe me, it's a major change.
With this update, you've witnessed the completion of TEKO's base content.

Obviously, I'm going to keep expanding everything. But for the next patch, I'm going to focus on something I left unfinished: aesthetics. I'm going to be working for a very long time. It'll probably take me several weeks to release u9.0. I'll take the time to leave the game as polished as possible.

Version u10.0 will probably be the "definitive" one; at that point, the game will feel incredibly good. After that, I'll keep releasing expansions with, specifically, more Cards and more Pockets, which are the most relevant content in TEKO.

We aren't close to the end of EA. I'm not going to rush this. It might be months away. I'm saving money to pay for resources and tools to make the game grow, so, don't doubt it: even if everything is finished, I don't plan on leaving EA, because first I have to work more on marketing. I haven't worked on this at all. I don't want to abandon the game or do something half-baked, which is why I've dedicated 95% of my time to programming/designing in-game. I've neglected the other things a lot, so at some point when everything feels stable, I'll need a few months to properly promote the game.

I have a lot of fun polishing TEKO. It's likely I'll release many small patches, with meticulous fixes. Every time I release new content I have to review the interactions again, this process is a bit slow. So, I know that when I move beyond u10.0 I'm going to have to invest a large chunk of time into pure testing.

I'm more ready than ever. Maybe I'm a disaster at marketing and a failure since this isn't succeeding, but my goal is clear: to entertain myself working on this, to create a 100% playable and polished product, and to fulfill my initial promise which was creating the game of my dreams. My favorite genre is Deckbuilders, this is something I do for love rather than money, and that's why I keep going even though I haven't earned anything. Is it a shame? Yes. But there are things you can't control. What can I control? The development. I'm going to be a better version of myself every time I can, don't doubt it. The day I feel TEKO is finished, bug-free, and only lacking optional content expansion, I'll be more than ready for the next step.

u.7.0.0!

21 new Consumables:
4 Common / 12 Rare / 5 Epic.

Consumable changes:
  • Outlay: +10 base -> +16 base.
  • Ticket: Epic -> Rare.
  • Shovel: NEW! 10% chance to drop a Common Sinister Card. Now you can only use this Consumable in the shop.
  • Mask: Fixed the description (instead of "common card" it said "normal card").
New mechanic: Sinister.
  • Cards that are Sinister won't take up any slots. This means you can get infinite Cards, slots are no longer a limitation.
  • You can't blend Sinister Cards.
  • Now Forbidden Cards won't take up space because they'll all be Sinister, so they won't delete the leftmost Card anymore.
Fixes:
  • Visual rework to Card management in the inventory, the drag animation, the arrangement, and position calculation. When hovering over a Card, it now appears on top of the others if they're too close together. Having more than 12 Cards makes the system change completely so it's not uncomfortable to manage them. Besides, I remade the Mod management from scratch (transferring/equipping/unequipping them should be easier when we have a lot of Cards). Cards will get smaller and separate from each other when we need to interact with them, otherwise they'll be grouped together, one on top of the other.
  • Linen Pocket no longer acts like Outlaw Pocket. That was a huge mistake. The logic for the 2 Pockets got mixed up. It's fixed now.
  • The order of consumables and Mods in the Codex has been fixed. Now they display correctly depending on their rarity, from highest to lowest.
  • The Cross Sticker is working now, it should give the Consumable/Sticker correctly when discarding it.
  • Improved the name color in the tooltip for Stickers that have an individual trait.
  • Purchased consumables will give $0 when sold.
  • Fixed Flowar Boss, it wasn't working before. Now it correctly blocks a random Action Card.

I've created a basic guide with super hidden pro tips for everyone who just started playing the game, I highly recommend checking it out, it's completely free: LINK. Yes, it's on Patreon, but it's a FREE post. I recommend following me there, I started making posts visible to everyone. Sometimes I publish paid content, but I also think about the people who can't pay. I upload very interesting stuff, whether it's about my life as a dev, tips, lore, and teasers. I love writing.

• Fixed a visual bug: Starlight Chips now appear with the Noise/Grain effect in the shop; previously they appeared gray.
  • Numberless/Ultranumber descriptions no longer duplicate in chip tooltips.
  • Modified tooltip title colors. Previously, all trait titles were the same purple color; now each has a distinct color. For example, if a chip is 'Ultracolor' and 'Shapeless' and also has a 'Knife Sticker', the titles of those three traits will each have different colors instead of all being purple.
  • If the player has Last Drink Card, Lino will now remove -$5. Previously this didn't work, making it easy to bypass this boss debuff.
  • Confirmed: chips with Knife Sticker CAN remove Numberless/Ultranumber chips.

A LOT OF BUFFS.
I've just made the most generous patch in the game! I hope it doesn't make things too easy, otherwise I'll have to adjust more. I want this to be balanced and for the winrate to stabilize. I obviously want players to win more runs, and I've realized the game has been unfair. I agree that balance still needs work, and I'll keep taking feedback. If I see that the winrate improves without getting out of control, I won't nerf the mechanics, I'll leave them as they are.

GENERAL BUFFS:
  • It's now easier to play with higher max mana. Previously, I had implemented a mechanic that heavily penalized this. This is one of the most important changes, allowing players to accumulate more resources and scale much more easily.
  • Playing with more mana in D3 and D4 will be even easier. This is because the mechanics in these higher difficulties make it more punishing to have low mana, making it one of the most valuable stats.
  • Starting from round 21, it's now also possible to earn additional money (there's a passive bonus for winning rounds; it was previously penalized, but now all runs beyond round 22 will earn money as well, including in Endless mode).
  • Increased general Initial Money (the amount players start runs with).
  • Special Money bonus in D4. Important for scaling better against bosses, as their effects are very punishing.
  • Reduced mod costs in D3 and D4 (-$1).
  • Chips with two traits at once (special color and shape) now cost $1 less.
  • Reduced Score Goal and Overkill scaling in D4.
  • Reduced Pro Mod cost to $9.
SPECIFIC BUFFS:
  • Wood Pocket: -1 card cost. Players now start with 7 unlocked card slots instead of 5. Reduced cost of all card slots.
  • Forbidden Pocket: reduced Score Goal and Overkill increase percentages.
  • Hacker Pocket: increased Initial Money and +1 efficiency to all colored tubes.
  • Warlock/Chosen Pockets: restored Initial Money. Previously, they gave $0 to offset their strength.
  • Outlaw Pocket: reduced Overkill penalty.
  • Ruin Pocket: increased chances for Cards/Stickers.
  • Oily Pocket: reduced card cost, it was unnecessarily high.
  • Linen Pocket: buffed eco divisor ($1 every $3).
  • Drab Pocket: more Initial Money.
  • Empanada Pocket: more Initial Money.
BUG FIXES:
  • Fixed crashes that ULTRANUMBER was causing. Also, ULTRANUMBER/NUMBERLESS should now position correctly in hand when discarding/playing chips and during draw animations.
  • Fixed Lankvian bug, it can no longer convert ULTRANUMBER/NUMBERLESS.

Fixed a crash when using a Delete Pack while having at least one Ultranumber chip. This trait may still cause issues.
Fixed a bug where Mods were not contributing to scoring.

There may still be more bugs related to chip/sticker interactions, as well as the scoring execution order. Overall things are fairly clean, but keep an eye on those two aspects of the game.
